title: Origin of seed plants
summary: Earlier land plants reproduced by spores, as mosses and ferns still do. The seed let plants colonise environments that had been unsuitable. The oldest known seeds, borne in branching cupules, come from Late Devonian (Famennian) rocks of the Hampshire Formation in Randolph County, West Virginia; the plant, Elkinsia polymorpha, grew in swamps on an ancient coastal plain and is the oldest seed plant known in North America. By the Mississippian and Pennsylvanian, from 345 million years ago, seed plants spread as great forests across much of the earth.

uncertainty.note: Nature (Gillespie et al. 1981) dates the seeds to the Famennian (Fa2c) stage of the Late Devonian without a numeric age; the West Virginia Encyclopedia dates the seed-plant forests of the Mississippian and Pennsylvanian to 345-280 million years ago.

importance.justification: The seed let plants conquer dry land, leading to forests, conifers and flowering plants (R4 D3 T4 L3).

related.because: The initial colonization of land by non-vascular and early vascular plants provided the ancestral lineage and terrestrial soils from which seed plants evolved.

beats.caption: Early seed plants such as Elkinsia polymorpha evolve cupulate ovules along coastal wetlands of Laurussia.
Seed-bearing plants spread across continental interiors, initiating the global diversification of gymnosperms.
